title: Stackification commutes with two-fibre products of fibred groupoids
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and a site $(\mathcal C,J)$ [def-weil-pbc-topos] small in the larger universe. Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal Z$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C$, with fibre groupoids in that universe, and let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $g:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ be functors over $\mathcal C$ preserving cartesian arrows. Here a cartesian arrow is an arrow with the unique lifting property for factorizations over base arrows; being fibred in groupoids means that such lifts exist with every prescribed target, and every fibre is a groupoid. Form $\mathcal P=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ fibrewise: its objects over $T$ are triples $(x,z,\alpha:f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}g(z))$ and its arrows are pairs $(a:x\to x',b:z\to z')$ satisfying $g(b)\alpha=\alpha'f(a)$; pullbacks are induced by those of the factors. Let $a_J$ denote stackification with the arrow-sheafification and local-image properties of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. There is an equivalence over $\mathcal C$
$$a_J(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z)\simeq a_J\mathcal X\times_{a_J\mathcal Y}a_J\mathcal Z,$$
whose composite with the stackification map from $\mathcal P$ is, up to a natural isomorphism over the identity of the base, the functor induced by the three stackification maps. This equivalence commutes with both projections and the comparison isomorphism between their images in $a_J\mathcal Y$. If a factor is already a $J$-stack (isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and covering descent data for objects are effective), its stackification can be taken to be itself, with the identity map.

source.place: Tag 04Y2 (lemma-stackification-fibre-product-categories-fibred-in-groupoids), via Tag 04Y1 (lemma-stackification-fibre-product-fibred-categories), including its canonical comparison.

proof.text: Write $i_X,i_Y,i_Z$ for the stackification maps. Extend $i_Yf$ and $i_Yg$ using [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], obtaining $f^a:a_J\mathcal X\to a_J\mathcal Y$, $g^a:a_J\mathcal Z\to a_J\mathcal Y$ and comparisons $\epsilon_X:f^ai_X\cong i_Yf$, $\epsilon_Z:g^ai_Z\cong i_Yg$. By [lem-sfb-stack-groupoid-two-fibre-products], $\mathcal Q=a_J\mathcal X\times_{a_J\mathcal Y}a_J\mathcal Z$ is a stack. Define $k:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ by $k(x,z,\alpha)=(i_Xx,i_Zz,\epsilon_Z^{-1}i_Y(\alpha)\epsilon_X)$ and $k(a,b)=(i_Xa,i_Zb)$. Naturality of the comparisons gives the required square for arrows, and their pullback compatibility gives that of $k$. Extend $k$ to $h:\mathcal W=a_J\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ with $h i_P\cong k$ using the same stackification lemma.

For $p=(x,z,\alpha)$ and $p'=(x',z',\alpha')$ over $T$, let $A=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(x,x')$, $B=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Z}(z,z')$, $C=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(fx,gz')$ be presheaves on $\mathcal C/T$. The maps to $C$ are $a\mapsto\alpha'f(a)$ and $b\mapsto g(b)\alpha$. Thus $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal P}(p,p')=A\times_C B$ by the defining square. The arrow-sheafification clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] identifies $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal W}(i_Pp,i_Pp')$ with $(A\times_C B)^\#$. The same clause in the three factors identifies $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Q}(kp,kp')$ with $A^\#\times_{C^\#}B^\#$, using the comparisons $\epsilon_X,\epsilon_Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] applied on the small slice site these are canonically isomorphic. This is the map induced by $h$: its composites with both projections are the sheafifications of those induced by $k$, which determine the map into the fibre product.

For arbitrary $w,w'\in\mathcal W(T)$, the local-image clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] gives a common covering sieve on which they are isomorphic to $i_Pp,i_Pp'$. A common covering sieve exists by intersection and transitivity of the topology; this uses no fibre products of base objects. The preceding step makes the map of their isomorphism sheaves bijective on every such restriction. To lift an arrow globally, lift its restrictions uniquely; uniqueness makes these lifts agree on every further restriction, so the source isomorphism sheaf glues them. Equality is likewise detected on this covering sieve. Consequently $h_T$ is fully faithful for every $T$.

Let $q=(\xi,\zeta,\gamma)\in\mathcal Q(T)$. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], after successive coverings choose $x\in\mathcal X$, $z\in\mathcal Z$ and isomorphisms $s:i_Xx\to\xi$, $t:i_Zz\to\zeta$. Then $\delta=\epsilon_Z g^a(t)^{-1}\gamma f^a(s)\epsilon_X^{-1}$ is an isomorphism $i_Yfx\to i_Ygz$. It is a section of the sheafification of $I=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(fx,gz)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-large-set-sheafification], the unit $I\to I^\#$ is locally bijective: its sheafification is an isomorphism by the universal property of sheafification. In particular, after a further covering $\delta=i_Y(\alpha)$ for $\alpha:fx\to gz$. Thus $(s,t)$ is an isomorphism $k(x,z,\alpha)\to q$. Transitivity of $J$ combines the successive coverings. Hence $q$ is locally in the essential image of $k$, and therefore of $h$. The source and target of $h$ are stacks and its fibre functors are fully faithful by the preceding step. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] to conclude that $h$ is an equivalence over $\mathcal C$.

We verify the projection and 2-cell compatibility, including the choice of their extensions. Let $p_X^a:\mathcal W\to a_J\mathcal X$ and $p_Z^a:\mathcal W\to a_J\mathcal Z$ be extensions of $i_Xp_X$ and $i_Zp_Z$. On $i_P(\mathcal P)$, the isomorphism $hi_P\cong k$ supplies comparisons $\operatorname{pr}_Xh\cong p_X^a$ and $\operatorname{pr}_Zh\cong p_Z^a$. For general $w$, take local representatives $w\cong i_Pp$ and conjugate these components by the representative isomorphisms. On overlaps the change of representative is an arrow between images of objects of $\mathcal P$; the arrow-sheafification clause makes it locally an image of an arrow of $\mathcal P$, by [lem-weil-pbc-large-set-sheafification]. Naturality on $\mathcal P$ therefore makes the components agree locally and hence agree in the target isomorphism sheaf. They glue uniquely. The same argument for arrows proves naturality and for base restriction proves pullback compatibility. Apply this also to $f^ap_X^a$ and $g^ap_Z^a$ to extend the comparison 2-cell. Its equality with the tautological 2-cell after these projection comparisons holds on $i_Pp$ by the formula for $k$, hence holds globally by local representatives and separatedness. Thus the equivalence has all the stipulated compatibilities.

If a factor $\mathcal A$ is already a stack, its identity functor has the required stackification properties: its isomorphism presheaves are already sheaves, every object is itself in its image, and every functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Y$ extends along the identity as $F$. Thus in the preceding construction that factor's stackification and stackification map may be taken to be $\mathcal A$ and its identity.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q07-942c41d95 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and the new node in full, and Stacks 04Y1 (with its proof), 04Y2, 026G (with its proof), 02ZL, 02ZP and 0436. The item statement is unchanged from live, and live is still unsplit, so nothing supersedes this split. There is no repair note and no SGA. Steps 1-4 follow the 04Y1 proof. In step 1 the arrow square for k reduces to the P-square by naturality of ε. In step 2 Isom_P = A×_C B with the conjugated maps (checked), and the 00WJ exactness leaf gives (A×_C B)^# ≅ A^#×_{C^#}B^#. Step 3 is local bijectivity glued over common covering sieves. In step 4 I checked δ map by map, and the lifted pair (s,t) satisfies the arrow equation in Q. The large-set node, applied to the unit I→I^#, gives local surjectivity, and the 046N hypotheses (both sides stacks, h pullback-compatible, fibres fully faithful) all hold. Step 5 builds the 2-cell extension by hand using local representatives and separatedness, which is needed because the local-description node states no uniqueness. Step 6 (identity stackification of a stack) is elementary. The new node lem-sfb-stack-groupoid-two-fibre-products (026G/02ZL) is statement-only and self-contained, with correct tags and blueprint.from. It is true: Isom is a fibre product of sheaves, and descent splits into the two factors plus gluing in Isom. I tested it on the trivial topology, a terminal D, an empty factor and the empty covering sieve. It is not a clause of the item. My own grep for 026G/02ZL/04Y*, and a scan of statements on the live DAG, find only 04T2 (algebraic stacks) and unrelated Kerodon-02ZL nodes, so it is no duplicate. Mathlib IsStack has no 2-fibre-product result. I accept the tool_use of lem-weil-pbc-large-set-sheafification as a generic black box. No fixes.
